evals.name: review-notifications-module
evals.prompt: I'm about to open a PR that adds a notifications module to our backend. The module lives in evals/fixtures/notifications-pr/server/src/modules/notifications/ (treat evals/fixtures/notifications-pr/ as the repo root). Please review it for architecture problems. For every problem give the file, the offending line or import, why it is a problem and how to fix it. Write the review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: Three findings: routes.ts reads the database directly through the db client instead of going through the service; service.ts imports the octokit SDK directly instead of using the GitHub port; service.ts exposes a Drizzle $inferSelect row type (NotificationRow) in a public method signature. repository.ts and helpers.ts are clean.
expectations: review.md flags routes.ts for querying the database directly (the db client / drizzle-orm imports and the /notifications/unread handler) instead of calling the service
review.md flags service.ts for importing and constructing octokit directly, and recommends using the GitHubClient port obtained through the container

review.md flags the Drizzle row type NotificationRow (typeof ...$inferSelect) leaking out of service.ts via getLatestRow, and recommends returning a shared/domain type mapped in repository.ts or helpers.ts
review.md does NOT report repository.ts or helpers.ts importing drizzle-orm / the schema as a violation

evals.name: review-summaries-module
evals.prompt: Please review the new summaries feature before I send the PR. The module is in evals/fixtures/summaries-pr/server/src/modules/summaries/ and it also touched a shared contract file, evals/fixtures/summaries-pr/server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/summary.ts (treat evals/fixtures/summaries-pr/ as the repo root). List every architecture problem with file, why it is wrong and the fix, and write it to review.md.
evals.expected_output: Three findings: service.ts constructs an OpenAI client directly instead of using the LLMProvider port from the container; the shared contract summary.ts imports from server modules (domain depending outward); routes.ts holds business logic (free-tier quota check, empty-diff validation, direct repository use) that belongs in service.ts. repository.ts is clean.
expectations: review.md flags service.ts for importing the openai SDK and calling new OpenAI(...) inside the service, and recommends the LLMProvider port resolved through the container (so it can be mocked via ContainerOverrides)
review.md flags contracts/summary.ts for importing from modules/summaries/helpers.js, i.e. the shared domain layer depending on server code
review.md flags routes.ts for containing business logic (the free-plan daily limit check and/or empty-diff validation) and for using SummaryRepository directly, and says this belongs in service.ts
review.md does NOT report repository.ts as a violation

evals.name: add-slack-integration
evals.prompt: Add a Slack notification: when a review finishes, post a short message to a Slack incoming-webhook URL (read from the secrets provider under the name SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL). The project is in evals/fixtures/slack-feature/ (treat it as the repo root; do not edit it in place). Write every new or changed file into your outputs folder, keeping the same relative paths, and add a short NOTES.md listing which files you created or changed.
evals.expected_output: A new SlackNotifier port in shared adapters.ts, a concrete implementation under server/src/adapters/slack/, a mock in adapters/mocks.ts, registration in platform/container.ts with an override and getter, and ReviewService calling it only through the container.
expectations: A new Slack-related interface (port) is added to server/src/vendor/shared/adapters.ts
The concrete implementation (the code that performs the HTTP call to the webhook) lives in a new file in its own new directory under server/src/adapters/<name>/
A mock implementation of the new port is added to server/src/adapters/mocks.ts
container.ts registers the new adapter with a getter and a ContainerOverrides entry
ReviewService reaches the notifier only through this.container and contains no fetch/axios/Slack SDK call or import of the concrete adapter

evals.name: review-invoices-repo-rules

review.md flags InvoiceService.create for exposing the Drizzle type typeof invoices.$inferInsert (imported from db/schema) in its public signature and recommends a shared/domain type instead
review.md does NOT present repository.ts as a violation

evals.name: review-orders-compliant-trap
evals.prompt: Please review the orders PR before I open it. The changed files are listed in evals/fixtures/orders-pr/CHANGED.txt and the repo snapshot is under evals/fixtures/orders-pr/ (treat it as the repo root). expectations: review.md concludes the PR has no blocking architecture/layering violation and is fine to merge on that front

review.md does NOT report OrderService taking the whole Container in its constructor, or building its repository with new OrderRepository(container.db), as a violation or something that must be changed
review.md does NOT report the cross-module call new CustomerService(this.container) as a violation, and does not demand injecting it through the constructor or a new container getter

The project is in evals/fixtures/review-to-notification/ (treat it as the repo root; do not edit it in place). Write every new or changed file into your outputs folder, keeping the same relative paths, and add a short NOTES.md listing which files you created or changed.
evals.expected_output: ReviewService instantiates NotificationService at the call site with new NotificationService(this.container) and calls record(). No new container getter or facade, no direct use of the notifications repository or schema from reviews, no unnecessary port/adapter.

No new getter or facade for the notifications service is added to container.ts
The reviews module does not import NotificationRepository or anything from db/schema for notifications

evals.name: scaffold-tags-module
evals.prompt: Add a tags feature: a repo can have tags (name and color). Users create, list and delete tags through REST endpoints; tags are stored in Postgres via Drizzle. The project is in evals/fixtures/tags-scaffold/ (treat it as the repo root; do not edit it in place). Write every new file into your outputs folder, keeping the same relative paths, and add a short NOTES.md listing the files you created and anything that has to be done outside server/.
evals.expected_output: Role-named module files under server/src/modules/tags/ (routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts, optional helpers.ts/constants.ts); service takes the whole Container and builds its own repository; routes only call the service; repository maps rows to a shared type; the Zod contract lives in server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/ and NOTES says it must be copied by hand to client/src/vendor/shared.
expectations: The module lives in server/src/modules/tags/ and its files are named by role (routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts, optionally helpers.ts and constants.ts), not by feature or pattern (no tags.controller.ts, tags.service.ts, dto/ or models/)
TagService takes the whole Container in its constructor and builds its own repository from container.db
routes.ts imports only its service, shared contracts, zod and fastify: no drizzle-orm, db client or schema, and each handler makes one service call
Public repository methods return a shared/domain Tag type, not a Drizzle $inferSelect row type
The Tag contract is a Zod schema under server/src/vendor/shared/contracts/ and NOTES.md says it must also be copied by hand to client/src/vendor/shared

evals.name: review-tickets-error-contract
evals.prompt: Please review the tickets PR before I open it. The changed files are listed in evals/fixtures/tickets-pr/CHANGED.txt and the (server-only) repo snapshot is under evals/fixtures/tickets-pr/ (treat it as the repo root). List every architecture problem with file, why it is a problem and how to fix it, and write the review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: Four findings about the failure path: routes.ts hand-builds a 404 body; routes.ts remaps error strings to statuses in a try/catch; service.ts throws bare Error('ticket_...') instead of AppError subclasses from platform/errors.ts; the Octokit adapter lets vendor exceptions escape instead of wrapping them in ExternalServiceError. repository.ts is fine.
expectations: review.md flags the GET /tickets/:id handler for building the 404 reply by hand (reply.code(404).send({ error: ... })) and recommends throwing NotFoundError from platform/errors.ts so the central error handler renders it
review.md flags the try/catch in POST /tickets/:id/close that maps error message strings to 404/409 by hand, and recommends the service throw AppError subclasses that the central error handler maps
review.md flags service.ts for throwing bare new Error('ticket_not_found') / new Error('ticket_already_closed') instead of AppError subclasses from platform/errors.ts
review.md flags the Octokit adapter (adapters/github/issues.ts) for letting the vendor exception escape and recommends wrapping failures in ExternalServiceError
review.md does NOT present repository.ts as a violation

evals.name: add-ticket-assign-errors
evals.prompt: Add POST /tickets/:id/assign with body { assignee }. It must assign the ticket in our database and on GitHub. Return a 404 if the ticket does not exist, reject the request if the ticket is already closed, and make sure a GitHub failure surfaces as an error to the caller. The project is in evals/fixtures/tickets-scaffold/ (treat it as the repo root; do not edit it in place). Write every new or changed file into your outputs folder, keeping the same relative paths, and add a short NOTES.md listing which files you created or changed.
evals.expected_output: Service throws NotFoundError for a missing ticket and ValidationError (or another AppError subclass) for a closed ticket; the GitHub adapter or service wraps failures in ExternalServiceError; routes.ts has no hand-built error replies or try/catch remapping; no bare Error is thrown anywhere in the new code.
expectations: A missing ticket is reported by throwing NotFoundError imported from platform/errors.ts
A closed ticket is rejected by throwing an AppError subclass from platform/errors.ts (for example ValidationError) in the service, not a bare Error and not a hand-built reply
routes.ts contains no hand-built 4xx/5xx reply body (no reply.code(4xx/5xx).send / reply.status(4xx/5xx).send) and no try/catch that remaps errors
A GitHub failure is wrapped in ExternalServiceError (in the adapter or the service) instead of letting the Octokit exception escape
No new or changed file contains a bare throw new Error(...)

evals.name: review-billing-deep-search
evals.prompt: Please review the billing PR before I open it. The changed files are listed in evals/fixtures/billing-pr/CHANGED.txt and the (server-only) repo snapshot is under evals/fixtures/billing-pr/ (treat it as the repo root). List every architecture problem with file, why it is a problem and how to fix it, and write the review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: Six indirect violations: service->helpers->db transitive leak; service imports another module's repository; billing<->customers service cycle; InvoiceRow ($inferSelect alias) in a service signature; lib/payments.ts Stripe wrapper used by the service; customers/routes.ts importing billing's repository. Decoys that must not be flagged: whole-Container constructor, own repository, one-way new NotificationService(this.container), repositories, pure formatAmount.
expectations: review.md reports that billing/service.ts reaches the database through helpers.ts (nextInvoiceNumber imports db/client.js and db/schema), naming helpers.ts as the leak or the chain service.ts -> helpers.ts -> db
review.md flags billing/service.ts importing and instantiating CustomerRepository from the customers module, and says the call must go through CustomerService
review.md flags the import cycle between billing/service.ts and customers/service.ts (BillingService <-> CustomerService)
review.md flags the Drizzle-derived alias InvoiceRow (billing/types.ts, typeof invoices.$inferSelect) used in BillingService.getRow's return type
review.md flags lib/payments.ts (module-level new Stripe(...) exported as stripe) being used directly by billing/service.ts and recommends a port/adapter wired through the container
review.md flags customers/routes.ts importing InvoiceRepository from the billing module and querying it directly instead of calling a service
review.md does NOT report as a violation: BillingService taking the whole Container, new InvoiceRepository(container.db), or the one-way new NotificationService(this.container) call
review.md does NOT report any repository.ts file or the pure formatAmount helper as a violation
